transcript.answer: Otto uses one server-held TMS API key because the delivered OLT TMS API supports nothing else. It authenticates every request with a single global `x-api-key` header. It has no user login, no OAuth flow and no per-user credential. So customers have no TMS credential to present, which rules out ADR-001's Option A (each user forwards their own credential). re:cinq has none to exchange or hold either, which rules out Option B. The key is company-scoped, not user-scoped, and it is the same for every user in the company. That leaves Option C, a server-held key with the customer boundary enforced in Otto's own code. A scope resolver (`apps/api/src/tools/toolAuth.ts`) derives the `customerNumber` from the authenticated customer company, never from the model or the request. Each TMS tool also runs an ownership check, so customers can only ask about their own bookings.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly says there is one global key, the customer boundary is enforced in Otto's code, and forwarding is impossible because the TMS has no user-level auth, but it never states that the TMS issues one key per integration partner, saying instead that the key is company-scoped and shared by every user in the company.
